failure: When more than one source-quality parent is contested, selectTargetParent currently counts any receipt carrying a matching targetRef+clauseRef before checking whether that receipt is a completed GUT contamination-triage receipt. A non-GUT, incomplete, provenance-empty, or non-decomposing receipt can therefore add a second matched parent and force MULTIPLE/HOLD, suppressing an otherwise valid single-parent GUT decomposition.
risk: Cross-organ noise can regulate VAJRA behavior without passing the same qualification boundary required to create decomposition. This is a denial/pollution path: an irrelevant receipt does not manufacture certainty, but it can block a valid behavior change and make routing depend on unrelated traffic.
requiredRepair: Multi-parent target selection must derive target candidates only from receipts that satisfy the bounded preconditions for GUT contamination triage, then run full parent-scoped qualification after selecting exactly one parent. Rejected noise must remain auditable and must not silently disappear.
requiredTests: valid GUT receipt for parent B plus non-GUT scoped noise for parent A still decomposes B
valid GUT receipt plus incomplete GUT noise on another parent still decomposes the valid parent
two genuinely qualifying GUT receipts targeting two parents still HOLD
no qualifying scoped target among multiple parents still HOLD
branch order and receipt order do not change the result
